articles.name: Virtual Mix Rack (VMR) vs. Virtual Modules (VMs): What's the Difference?
articles.title: Virtual Mix Rack (VMR) vs. Virtual Modules (VMs): What's the Difference?
articles.body:
Most of the modules in Virtual Mix Rack are also available as individual plugins called Virtual Modules, or VMs. They share names with their VMR counterparts, but they are separate plugins. This article explains the difference and why you may be asked to install a VM for something you already use in VMR, such as when opening a Playground session.

Quick Comparison

VMR Modules VMs (Virtual Modules)
What it is A module that loads inside Virtual Mix Rack An individual module released as its own plugin
Format Proprietary module format (.EPL), designed for VMR only VST2, VST3, AU, and AAX
Where it works Only inside Virtual Mix Rack Directly in your DAW, like any other plugin
How it appears Loaded from within the Virtual Mix Rack plugin Listed in your DAW with "VM" in front of the name (e.g., "VM FG-401")
What you need installed Virtual Mix Rack The specific VM plugin

What is a VMR module?

Modules in Virtual Mix Rack, such as the FG-401, use a proprietary module format (.EPL) that is designed to work only inside VMR. They can't be loaded outside of the Rack.

What is a VM?

VMs, or "Virtual Modules," are the individual modules of VMR broken out of the Rack and formatted as standalone plugins in VST2, VST3, AU, and AAX. They're for anyone who wants to use a module directly on a track without opening VMR.

How do I tell if I'm looking at a VM in my DAW?

Look for "VM" in front of the module name. In the example below from Reaper, each plugin is listed as "VM" followed by the module name (VM FG-401, VM FG-2A, and so on), shown here in both VST and VST3 formats.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do I need to install the VM if I already have the same module available in VMR?
Yes. The VMR module and the VM are treated as separate plugins, so having one doesn't cover the other.

Can I use the module from Virtual Mix Rack outside of the Rack?
If you want to use a module outside of Virtual Mix Rack, or have a session that a Virtual Module was used in, you'll need to install the Virtual Module version. Modules from the Virtual Mix Rack and Virtual Modules aren't interchangeable in your DAW.

Why does a Playground session ask me to install a plugin I already use in VMR?
Playground sessions are built with either the VMR version of a module or the VM version. If a session uses a VM, you need that VM installed, even if you have the same module in VMR.

Can I open Playground sessions without installing both versions of a plugin?
Unfortunately, no. If a session uses the Virtual Mix Rack version of a module, you'll need Virtual Mix Rack installed. If it uses a VM, you'll need that VM installed.

Why does Complete Access show a plugin as "not installed" when I use it in VMR?
The VMR module and the VM are separate plugins, so having a module in VMR doesn't count as having the VM installed.

Still need help?

If you have questions about VMR or VMs, contact the Slate Digital Support team by submitting a request here.

articles.name: Complete Access Free Trial Not Activating: Showing as "Revoked"
articles.title: Complete Access Free Trial Not Activating: Showing as "Revoked"
articles.body:
If you started a Complete Access free trial but your plugins won't activate (or display as "revoked"), this article explains why it happens, how to avoid it, and how our Support team can get you up and running.

Short version: If you've tried Complete Access before, always start a new trial with the same Slate Digital account and the same iLok ID. Using a different account or iLok ID on the same computer can cause iLok to block your trial licenses.

What you might see

Complete Access is made up of three collections, and each one appears as its own license in iLok:

  • Complete Access: Slate Digital
  • Complete Access: LiquidSonics
  • Complete Access: Solid State Logic

If your trial is affected, one or more of these collections can be blocked. On Mac or Windows, you might see:

  • A message saying "Some licenses could not be activated," naming the affected collections
  • A plugin, such as MetaTune or Virtual Mix Rack, reporting "License not found"
  • One or more collections listed as "Revoked" under iLok Licenses Status on your Complete Access subscription page
  • A trial that shows as active in your account, but plugins that still won't unlock

Results can be mixed. In the example below, Solid State Logic is activated while Slate Digital and LiquidSonics are revoked. If any collection shows "Revoked," your trial is affected, even if another one looks fine.


Example of a Complete Access subscription page with Slate Digital and LiquidSonics revoked and Solid State Logic activated.

Why this happens

The most common cause is a previous Complete Access trial on the same computer. iLok, the licensing system from PACE that protects our plugins, remembers when a trial has already been used on a computer. If a new trial is started there with a different Slate Digital account or iLok ID, iLok's fraud protection treats it as a possible duplicate trial and blocks the licenses from activating, even though the trial looks active in your account. This can happen without you meaning to, for example by signing up with a different email address or creating a new iLok account.

iLok also handles each collection separately, which is why results can be mixed. The customer in the example above had tried Slate Digital's Complete Access on its own in the past, back when the three collections weren't offered together. When they started a new trial later, iLok allowed only the Solid State Logic collection to activate.

How to avoid it

  • Use the same Slate Digital account (email address) you used for any earlier Complete Access trial, even one from before the three collections were combined.
  • Sign in to iLok with the same iLok User ID you used before.
  • Don't create a new Slate Digital account or iLok ID to start another trial on the same computer.

Not sure which account you used? Search your inbox for earlier emails from Slate Digital or iLok, or let us know and we'll help you track it down.

If your trial is already affected

  1. Submit a request and include:
    • The email address on your Slate Digital account
    • Your iLok User ID
    • A screenshot of the error, or of the iLok Licenses Status section on your subscription page
    • The email address or iLok ID from any earlier trial, if you remember it
  2. We'll review your trial history and either deposit replacement licenses to your iLok account or reset the trial on your original account.
  3. Open iLok License Manager, sign in with your iLok User ID, and look for the new licenses under the Available tab. If you don't see the tab, expand the window or click your username. Replacement licenses may list their Type as "NFR Subscription" instead of "Trial/Demo." That's expected.
  4. Activate the licenses by following Activating your subscription licenses in the iLok License Manager.

Good to know

  • Replacement licenses don't restart or extend your trial. Your original trial dates and billing terms still apply, so if you don't want to continue, cancel your subscription before the trial ends.
  • Free trials (resets) are typically available about once a year. If it's been a while since your last trial, you can usually try again, as long as you use your original Slate Digital account and iLok ID.

articles.name: Why Does My Subscription Say "Revoked"?
articles.title: Why Does My Subscription Say "Revoked"?
articles.body:
Quick answer: If you see a green Active subscription on your Subscriptions page, your subscription is fine. Any subscription marked Revoked in red is an old subscription that has already ended. You can ignore it.

Active means you are good to go. Revoked means it is a past subscription that has ended and can be ignored.

Important: The Active subscription is the only one that matters. A Revoked entry does not affect your licenses, your billing, or your access to plugins.

How many Active subscriptions should I see?

You should see as many green Active subscriptions as you expect to have. For most users, that is 1. If you have multiple subscriptions on purpose, for example, a studio with a subscription for each room, each one will show as Active. That is normal.

If you see more Active subscriptions than you intended, please contact our support team.

Why do I have Revoked subscriptions?

A subscription becomes Revoked once it ends. Some common reasons:

  • A previous plan was canceled or expired
  • A free trial ended and was converted to a new plan
  • You switched from one plan to another, for example, from a month-to-month All Access Pass to an annual Complete Access plan
  • A previous subscription was terminated after missed payments

Revoked subscriptions are never removed from the page, so the list can grow over time. This is normal.

Where do I check the status of my licenses?

Look inside your Active subscription. The iLok Licenses Status section lists each license and where it is activated. You can also check your monthly price, your next payment, your auto-renewal setting, and your payment method there.

What if I do not see a green Active subscription?

If every subscription on the page is marked Revoked, you do not currently have an active subscription.

If this was unexpected, your plan may have been terminated after a missed payment. Please review our Missed Subscription Payments: What Happens Next? article for the full retry schedule.

If you just redeemed a free trial and it shows as Revoked, please see this article 👇

📝 Complete Access Free Trial Not Activating: Showing as "Revoked"

If you would like to start a new subscription with the same account, you can do that on our Pick Your Plan page.

Still need help?

If you have any questions or need further assistance, feel free to contact our support team.

articles.title: Reporting a Security Vulnerability
articles.body:
What is product-security@slatedigital.com for?

product-security@slatedigital.com is our dedicated channel for reporting security vulnerabilities related to Slate Digital software or hardware. Reports sent to this address are reviewed by our Support team together with the relevant security and engineering teams, so issues reach the right people quickly.

When to contact this address

Use product-security@slatedigital.com if you believe you've found a security vulnerability affecting a Slate Digital product, including:

  • Our software, such as Complete Access plugins, VMS, or our licensing/activation systems
  • Our hardware, such as the ML-1, ML-1A, or ML-2A microphones
  • Our website or account systems, where the issue is security-related (e.g. a potential data exposure)

What to include in your report

To help us investigate as quickly as possible, please include:

  • A clear description of the vulnerability and its potential impact
  • The affected product and version
  • Steps to reproduce the issue, if possible
  • Any supporting details — logs, screenshots, or a proof of concept

What happens after you email us

Your report goes to our Support team, who loop in our security and engineering teams for review. We'll acknowledge your report and follow up as our investigation progresses.

When to use a different channel

This address is reserved specifically for security vulnerability reports. For anything else, please reach out the right way so we can help you faster:

Quick FAQ

Is this address monitored 24/7? 
No. Reports are reviewed by our team during business hours, but security reports are prioritized.

I'm not sure if my issue counts as a security vulnerability. Should I still email this address? 
If you're unsure, it's fine to reach out here, and we'll help route it appropriately. For non-security issues, a general support ticket will usually get you a faster answer.

Can I use this address for account or billing problems? 
No. For account, billing, or purchase issues, please submit a ticket or contact sales@slatedigital.com for pricing-related questions.

articles.name: Plugin Interfaces Appear Blank or Black in Logic Pro
articles.title: Plugin Interfaces Appear Blank or Black in Logic Pro
label_names: Blank or missing plugin UI in Logic
articles.body:
Symptom

When you open a plugin in Logic Pro, the plugin window opens and shows the plugin's name at the top, but the rest of the interface is completely blank or black. No knobs, controls, or meters are visible. Audio still passes through the plugin normally; only the visual interface fails to load.

This can affect Slate Digital plugins as well as plugins from other developers on the same system, and it typically shows up around the time of a macOS update (including recent macOS Tahoe releases).

Quick fix

In the cases we've investigated, this has been caused by having more than one copy of Logic Pro installed on the same Mac — for example, one in your Applications folder and a separate, full copy elsewhere (such as on your Desktop or in your Downloads folder).

To resolve it:

  1. Check your Desktop, Downloads folder, and any external or backup drives for another copy of Logic Pro.app.
  2. If you find one, delete it completely.
  3. Reinstall Logic Pro fresh from the Mac App Store, making sure it installs only into your Applications folder.
  4. Restart your Mac.
  5. Reopen your project and test the plugin again.

A shortcut is fine

One quick note: it's completely fine to have a Logic Pro shortcut on your Desktop or anywhere else, as long as it's just an alias pointing back to the copy in your Applications folder. You can actually drag and drop Logic Pro from the Application folder, and macOS will create an Alias automatically. See below:


The issue is specifically when there's a separate, full copy of Logic Pro somewhere else on the Mac, especially if it's a different version that's no longer being updated along with the main copy in Applications.

Not sure if what you have is an alias or a full copy? Select it in Finder and press Command + I. An alias will say "Alias" right under the name and list the original file's location; a full copy will show a regular file size and application details instead.

If this doesn't resolve it

If you've confirmed there's only one copy of Logic Pro on your system and you're still seeing blank plugin interfaces, please reach out to our support team and include:

  • A screenshot of the affected plugin window
  • Your macOS version (Apple menu > About This Mac)
  • A full system report: Apple menu > About This Mac > System Report > File > Save, then attach the saved file to your message

articles.name: Unable to Use Virtual Microphone System with ML-1/ML-2 Microphones?
articles.title: Unable to Use Virtual Microphone System with ML-1/ML-2 Microphones?
articles.body:
Applies to: ML-1 (original/legacy microphone)

  • ML-1 Microphone Discontinued

  • ML-2 Microphone Discontinued
     

Quick Answer

If you own an original ML-1 microphone, the Virtual Microphone System (VMS) plugin will show as unlicensed by default — even if you already have a valid, active ML-1 license. That's expected. Your ML-1 license unlocks content inside the Virtual Mix Rack (VMR) plugin, not VMS. Getting VMS working with an ML-1 requires either an active Complete Access subscription or a separate VMS license purchase.

Why This Happens

There have been two versions of this microphone, and each defaults to a different plugin:

  • ML-1 (original, legacy): No longer sold through Slate Digital or authorized resellers. Existing units now circulate secondhand between end users. It works with the Virtual Mix Rack (VMR) plugin out of the box; VMS is available, but as an additional purchase.
  • ML-1A/ML-2A (current models): The only version currently sold by authorized resellers. Includes a perpetual VMS license automatically — no extra purchase or subscription needed.

Because the two mics look similar and both use Slate Digital's microphone-modeling technology, this is a common mix-up. It comes up in two scenarios most often:

  • You purchased a used ML-1 secondhand, and a license came with it (transferred from the previous owner or newly issued).
  • You purchased a new ML-1 license directly from Slate Digital Support.

In both cases, the license itself works the same way — it activates content in VMR, not VMS.

Don't have a working ML-1 license yet? This article assumes you already have one active on your account. If you bought an ML-1 secondhand and haven't been able to register or transfer the license, see How Do I Sell or Transfer My ML-1 License to Another User? first.

What Your ML-1 License Includes by Default

An ML-1 license activates the following inside Virtual Mix Rack:

  • Classic Tubes (8 microphone models)
  • Virtual Preamp Collection (FG-76, FG-73)
  • Free Rack modules: Monster, Revival, Trimmer

Open Virtual Mix Rack and confirm these modules show as licensed. If VMS is what's installed instead of (or alongside) VMR, that mismatch is the likely source of a "unlicensed" message.

How to Get Virtual Microphone System Working with Your ML-1

You have two options:

  1. Subscribe to Complete Access — includes VMS access along with every mic model and plugin Slate Digital offers, for as long as the subscription stays active. 👉 Slate Digital | Complete Access Sign-Up Page
  2. Purchase a VMS perpetual license separately — a one-time purchase that unlocks VMS for your ML-1, including all current ML-1 expansions (Strongroom London, Radio France, Classic 87 FET, Blackbird Mics, Classic Tubes 3) plus any future ML-1-specific releases. 👉 Purchase Virtual Microphone System

Once purchased or subscribed, relaunch the plugin and select ML-1 as your source microphone.

If You'd Rather Not Purchase VMS

Your ML-1 works fully with Virtual Mix Rack at no extra cost — nothing further to buy. If VMS is installed but you don't plan to use it, you can uninstall it via the Complete Access Hub app (click the three dots next to the plugin and choose Uninstall) to avoid the confusion going forward.

Related Articles

  • ML-1 vs ML-1A: Which Plugin Do I Use?
  • Virtual Microphone System – Perpetual License FAQ
  • What Software Comes with the ML-1 Microphone?
  • How Do I Sell or Transfer My ML-1 License to Another User?

articles.name: Can I Keep My Software License After Selling My ML-1A or ML-2A?
articles.title: Can I Keep My Software License After Selling My ML-1A or ML-2A?
articles.body:
Short answer: No

Your ML-1A or ML-2A's software license is permanently tied to that specific microphone's hardware serial number. When you sell the microphone, the license must transfer to the new owner along with it. The two can't be separated. Once the transfer is complete, you will no longer have access to the plugin (Virtual Microphone System) under that license.

If you decide to purchase an ML-1A or ML-2A later on, that microphone will come with its own new license tied to its serial number. It would be a completely separate mic/license pairing, rather than a continuation of the one you have now.

How the license transfer works

Since each transfer requires us to verify the payment and manually move the software license to the new owner, it isn’t something that happens automatically. Our support team handles the transfer directly from start to finish. Steps outlined below:

  1. Open a support ticket letting us know you've sold your ML-1A or ML-2A and need the license transferred to the new owner.
  2. We'll send you a secure payment link for the $25.00 transfer fee directly through your ticket. (We don't publish this link publicly, since every transfer is manually reviewed on our end.)
  3. Complete payment, then reply to your ticket to confirm.
  4. We verify the payment, then:
    • Revoke the original license from your account
    • Issue a brand-new software code, sent to you through that same support ticket
  5. You're responsible for passing the new code along to the buyer. We send the replacement code to the seller, not directly to the buyer, so be sure to forward it once you receive it.
  6. The new owner redeems the code and registers the hardware serial number to their own Slate Digital/Complete Access account, completing the transfer.

A few important notes

  • We recommend handling the transfer through Slate Digital support rather than reassigning the license solely through iLok License Manager. Going through us ensures your Complete Access account information updates correctly too... not just the iLok side.
  • Once your original license is revoked, there's no way to retain use of the plugin while the hardware changes hands. The mic's serial number and its software license always travel together.
  • If you decide to pay for the license transfer later, just have your ticket number handy when you follow up. That’ll help us locate everything and get the transfer processed more quickly.

Can I share my license across multiple systems?

Each ML-1A or ML-2A includes a single VMS license with two activation slots — but both of those slots must live on one iLok ID, under one Slate Digital account.

  • You can use your two activations across two of your own systems, in any combination of supported activation types, as long as they're all on the same iLok ID. For example:
    • Two iLok USB dongles
    • Two Machine IDs (two computers)
    • One iLok dongle + one Cloud Session
    • One Machine ID + one Cloud Session
    • Any other mix of two supported activation types under that single iLok ID
  • You cannot split those two activations across two different iLok IDs or two different Slate Digital accounts. The license is intended for one user only, so it can’t be shared with someone else, even if you’re only using one of the two available activations yourself.

If you want someone else to have access to the plugin, the license needs to be formally transferred to their account (see above), not shared alongside yours.

articles.title: How to Change Your Complete Access Subscription Currency
articles.body:
Slate Digital now supports additional currencies in our online shop as part of our regional pricing options.

Regional pricing helps make Complete Access subscriptions and other Slate Digital products more consistent with local purchasing power in supported territories.

At this time, our shop supports the following currencies:

  • USD
  • EUR
  • GBP
  • TRY
  • KRW

Additional currencies may be added in the future.

Can I change the currency on my existing Complete Access subscription?

No. Existing Complete Access subscriptions cannot be converted from one currency to another.

If you currently have an active Complete Access subscription in USD and would like to subscribe using one of our supported local currencies, you will need to cancel your current subscription and then sign up again using the correct currency.

You can sign up for Complete Access here: 👉 Slate Digital Complete Access Sign-Up Page

Regional pricing eligibility

Local currency pricing is only available to customers who are located in the corresponding supported region.

To use a supported local currency, your billing address and payment method must be associated with that region. Our checkout system includes verification measures to confirm regional eligibility, so customers will only be able to complete a purchase in a local currency when the billing details and payment method match the selected region.

If you are unable to complete checkout in your local currency, please confirm that your billing address and payment method are both tied to the correct region.

Will I receive a refund for past monthly payments?

No. We are not able to retroactively refund previous monthly subscription payments because a different currency or regional price is now available.

What if I already paid for a full year upfront?

If you paid for an annual Complete Access subscription upfront and are still mid-cycle, please contact Slate Digital Support. We can review the situation and see what options may be available.

You can contact us here:

Contact Slate Digital Support

articles.name: How to Redeem a Slate Digital Software Voucher (Purchased from a Reseller)
articles.title: How to Redeem a Slate Digital Software Voucher (Purchased from a Reseller)
articles.body:
If you purchased a Slate Digital plugin from an official reseller such as Plugin Boutique or Sweetwater, you will need to redeem a software voucher code to receive your license.

Before getting started:

  • After purchase, your reseller should provide you with a voucher code (usually via email).
  • If you have not received your code, you will need to contact the reseller directly.
  • Each voucher can only be used once and must be redeemed before you can access the plugin.

All Slate Digital vouchers are redeemed here:
👉 https://app.completeaccess.audio/gift

Note: Only one voucher can be redeemed at a time. If you purchased multiple products, repeat this process for each code.

Step 1 – Log In or Create an Account

When visiting the redemption page for the first time, you will be prompted to either log in or create an account.

  • If you already have a Slate Digital account, switch to Log in and enter your credentials.
  • If not, select Sign up and create an account using:
    • Email + password
    • OR Google, Facebook, or Apple login

Step 2 – Enter Your Voucher Code

Paste your voucher code into the field and click Redeem.

Example code: RM7F8XN6QYEP6B5F

Step 3 – Confirm Redemption

You’ll be taken to a checkout-style page showing your product.

  • The total due today should display as Free
  • Check the box to accept:
    • Audiotonix Terms & Privacy Policy
    • iLok Terms & Privacy Policy
  • Click Get This Product

Step 4 – Confirm Your Email Address (New Users Only)

If you just created an account, you must confirm your email address.

  • Check your inbox for the confirmation email
  • Click the Confirm My Email button


Important:

  • If your email is not confirmed, the voucher will not complete redemption
  • If you entered the wrong email, you will need to contact support
  • Vouchers cannot be reused or transferred to another account once redeemed

Existing users can skip this step.

Step 5 – Connect Your iLok Account

Once logged in, you’ll be taken to your Dashboard.

At the top of the page, click the “Connect iLok account” button in the purple banner.

Note: If you don't see "Connect iLok account" after your voucher has been redeemed, this means that you already have a valid iLok ID linked. You can skip to Step 7.

You’ll have two options:

Option A – Create a New iLok Account

Select:
“I don’t have an iLok account. Let’s create one for me”

  • This will create an iLok ID using your Slate Digital account email

Option B – Use an Existing iLok Account

Select:
“I already have an iLok account”

  • Enter your iLok User ID and password

Important:
Your iLok ID is not always your email address. Many users create a custom username (for example: producer123).

Step 6 – License Deposited

Once your iLok account is connected:

  • Your license is automatically deposited
  • You’ll see a confirmation message

Step 7 – Install and Activate Your Plugin

You’ll now be directed to download installers:

👉 https://app.completeaccess.audio/installers

You have two options:

Option A – Use Complete Access Hub (Recommended)

  • Download and install the app
  • Sign in with your Slate Digital account
  • Click Activate Licenses

This method helps keep your plugins up to date.

Option B – Manual Installation + iLok License Manager

If installing manually or using an iLok dongle:

  • Download your plugin installer directly
  • Activate your license using the iLok License Manager

See:
How to Activate Slate Digital Plugins to an iLok Dongle

articles.name: VMR 3 vs Mix Bundle One – What’s the Difference?
articles.title: VMR 3 vs Mix Bundle One – What’s the Difference?
articles.body:
This is a very common point of confusion, so let’s break it down.

What is VMR 3.0?

Virtual Mix Rack (VMR) is a plugin or 'module' host.

  • It allows you to load and chain different processing modules (EQs, compressors, etc.) inside a single interface
  • "VMR 3.0" simply refers to the current version of the plugin
  • It includes features like Macros and the Discovery Preset Browser

Important: VMR itself does not come with a full set of modules by default. What you can use inside VMR depends on the licenses you own.

What is Mix Bundle One?

Mix Bundle One is a bundle of modules that run inside VMR.

It includes the following:

  • FG-S (SSL-style EQ)
  • FG-N (Neve-style EQ)
  • FG-116 (1176-style compressor)
  • FG-401 (VCA compressor)

When you own Mix Bundle One, these are the modules that will be available to you inside VMR.

Free Modules Included with VMR

The following modules are free and included with any VMR setup:

  • Trimmer
  • Revival
  • Monster

These can also be redeemed separately for free here:

https://app.slatedigital.com/checkout?catalogItemReferenceId=vmr&bundleProductReference=revival

Key Takeaway

  • VMR (Virtual Mix Rack) = the plugin (host)
  • Mix Bundle One = a set of modules used inside VMR

They are not the same thing, but they work together.

Want More Modules?

VMR supports many additional modules beyond Mix Bundle One. To access more, you can:

  • Purchase additional bundles
  • Subscribe to the Complete Access plan for full access

If you're unsure what you own or what’s included in your account, feel free to reach out to our support team—we’re happy to help.

articles.name: Virtu: How Reference Tracks, Styles, and Mastering Credits Work
articles.title: Virtu: How Reference Tracks, Styles, and Mastering Credits Work
articles.body:
This article explains how reference tracks interact with Virtu's processing, how the Advanced Controls behave, and why mastering credits may appear on the website but not in the desktop app.

How does uploading a reference track impact my uploaded track?

Uploading a reference track changes the Style Virtu uses to analyze and process your track.

When a reference track is uploaded:

  • The reference track becomes the active Style.
  • Any previously selected style (such as Pop or Universal) is replaced.
  • Virtu analyzes the reference track and builds a suggested EQ curve and loudness target based on it.

Because the algorithm changes how it approaches your audio when a reference track is used, the overall processing behavior may change even though your Advanced Control settings remain available.

Recommended workflow when using a reference track

For the most predictable results, we recommend the following workflow:

  1. Upload your source track.
  2. Upload your reference track so Virtu can establish the style.
  3. Then adjust the Advanced Controls (EQ, compression, width, etc.) to fine-tune the result.

If you change the style or upload a different reference track after making adjustments, it is recommended to revisit and tweak the Advanced Controls again.

Why do I see mastering credits on the website but not in the desktop app?

Virtu is available in two versions, and they handle mastering credits differently.

Desktop Application

  • No mastering credits are required.
  • You can master unlimited tracks locally.
  • This is why credit information does not appear inside the desktop app.

Web Version

  • Uses cloud-based processing and storage.
  • Mastering uses credits.
  • Complete Access Bundle subscribers receive 3 free mastering credits per month.

These credits are what you see displayed on the Virtu website.

Which version should I use?

  • If you want unlimited mastering with no credits, the desktop app is usually the best option.
  • If you prefer cloud-based mastering and storage, you can use the web version and apply mastering credits.

Still have questions?

If you have any additional questions about Virtu or mastering workflows, please contact Slate Digital Support.

articles.name: Virtu: Does It Change Bit Depth or Apply Dithering?
articles.title: Virtu: Does It Change Bit Depth or Apply Dithering?
articles.body:
This article explains how Virtu handles bit depth during mastering and whether dithering is applied during export.

Important: This information applies to both versions of Virtu: the web-based version and the desktop application.

Does Virtu change the bit depth of my file?

No. Virtu exports your master using the same bit depth as the file that was originally uploaded.

For example:

  • If you upload a 16‑bit file, the exported master will remain 16‑bit.
  • If you upload a 24‑bit file, the exported master will remain 24‑bit.

Virtu does not currently include options to change bit depth during export.

Does Virtu apply dithering?

No. Virtu does not apply dithering during the mastering or export process.

If you need to convert a 24‑bit master to 16‑bit with dithering, this should be done after exporting from Virtu using your DAW or a mastering tool that supports dithering.

This workflow is common in mastering because dithering is typically applied at the very final stage when preparing a file for a specific delivery format.

Do I still need to deliver 16‑bit masters?

In most modern distribution workflows, 24‑bit masters are widely accepted and often preferred. Many streaming platforms now support high‑resolution audio files.

Examples include:

  • DistroKid – Accepts both 16‑bit and 24‑bit WAV files (up to 24‑bit / 96 kHz).
  • Spotify – Supports high‑resolution masters and uses 24‑bit files for newer lossless tiers.
  • Apple Music – Streams audio from 16‑bit / 44.1 kHz up to 24‑bit / 192 kHz.
  • Tidal and Amazon Music – Prioritize 24‑bit files for their highest‑quality streaming tiers.

When is 16‑bit still required?

The main scenario where 16‑bit / 44.1 kHz is still required is for physical CD production (Red Book CD standard).

Some older playback systems or niche digital stores may also request 16‑bit files for compatibility.

Recommended Virtu workflow

  1. Export your mix at the highest available quality (typically 24‑bit WAV).
  2. Upload the file to Virtu for mastering.
  3. Download the mastered file from Virtu.
  4. If needed, create a 16‑bit dithered version in your DAW for CD production or specific delivery requirements.

Still have questions?

If you have questions about mastering workflows or exporting files with Virtu, please contact Slate Digital Support.

What is the ML-2A?

The ML-2A is Slate Digital’s latest small-diaphragm condenser modeling microphone. It is the successor to the legacy ML-2 and represents a major upgrade in both hardware design and software capabilities when used with the Slate Digital Virtual Microphone System (VMS).

Can I use the ML-2A in Virtual Mix Rack?

No. The ML-2A is designed to be used with the Slate Digital Virtual Microphone System plugin and its extended feature set. It is not supported in Virtual Mix Rack.

The ML-2A is available as a matched stereo pair. At this time, it is sold as a pair only and cannot be purchased individually.

The ML-2A has a self-noise rating of 16 dB (A-weighted).

Yes. The ML-2A requires standard 48 V phantom power.

The ML-2A includes 36 microphone models out of the box when used with the Slate Digital VMS software, including the Radio France Instruments and Drum Pack collections.

The ML-2A introduces several key upgrades, including:

articles.name: FG-X Machine-ID Activation Limitations on Apple Silicon Macs
articles.title: FG-X Machine-ID Activation Limitations on Apple Silicon Macs
articles.body:
The original FG-X is a legacy Slate Digital product and behaves differently from newer Slate Digital plugins when it comes to activation. If you are subscribed to Complete Access and notice that FG-X asks for activation every time you launch your DAW, this article explains why and how to resolve it.

Why FG-X Cannot Use Machine-ID Activation

FG-X was discontinued before Slate Digital implemented Machine-ID (computer) activations across our plugin lineup. Because of this, the original FG-X can only be activated on a physical iLok 2 or iLok 3 USB dongle. Machine-ID activation is not supported for this plugin.

When FG-X is activated on an iLok dongle, it will function normally on any computer where the dongle is connected. If the dongle is not connected, FG-X will prompt for activation even if your subscription is active and other plugins authorize correctly.

Important: FG-X is part of our legacy product lineup and is no longer updated. The recommended replacement is FG-X 2, which supports Machine-ID activation and runs natively on Apple Silicon.

Using FG-X on Apple Silicon Macs

The original FG-X was never ported to run natively on Apple Silicon. If you need to open older sessions that used FG-X, you must run your DAW in Rosetta mode in order for the plugin to load.

How to Run Your DAW Using Rosetta

  1. Open your Applications folder.
  2. Right-click your DAW application.
  3. Select Get Info.
  4. Enable the option Open using Rosetta.
  5. Relaunch your DAW.

This allows the legacy FG-X plugin to function on Apple Silicon systems, but it is only needed for older sessions that still contain FG-X.

Recommended Path Forward

  • Use FG-X 2 for all new mixing and mastering projects.
  • Only use the legacy FG-X when reopening older sessions that require it.
  • Keep a physical iLok dongle available if you need access to the legacy FG-X.

You can learn more about both versions of the limiter here:

👉 FG-X and FG-X 2 Frequently Asked Questions

articles.name: Virtual Mix Rack Missing in Cubase After Updating? (VST2 vs VST3)
articles.title: Virtual Mix Rack Missing in Cubase After Updating? (VST2 vs VST3)
label_names: The plug-in "Virtual Mix Rack" could not be found - Cubase
articles.body:
The plug-in "Virtual Mix Rack" could not be found

If Virtual Mix Rack (VMR) shows as Missing in older Cubase projects after updating with Complete Access Hub (formerly known as Slate Digital Connect), it is almost always a plugin format issue, not an “old vs new” version. Cubase is trying to recall a format that is not currently available on your system.

Quick takeaway: VST2 and VST3 are different plugin formats. Sessions that were created with VST2 need the VST2 format available to recall those instances. Newer installs default to VST3, which Cubase may not substitute automatically in older versions.

Why Cubase Shows “Missing” (VST2 vs VST3 Recall)

❗ VST2 and VST3 are not interchangeable in Cubase 10 era projects. If the session used VST2 and that format is not installed or not scanned, VMR will appear missing even though you can add new VMR instances (VST3) to tracks.

Good news for Cubase 14 users

✅ Cubase 14 can automatically replace a missing VST2 instance of VMR with the installed VST3 version, showing a message like:

“The plug-in Virtual Mix Rack could not be found. It has automatically been replaced by the plug-in ‘Virtual Mix Rack’ version ‘[installed version number]’ in your project.”

How to Identify VST2 vs VST3 in Cubase

🔎 In the Cubase plug-in browser, VST3 plug-ins show three forward slashes /// next to the name. VST2 entries do not show slashes.

Check Your Installation Paths (Windows)

Confirm both formats are installed in the expected locations. By default, our installers and Complete Access Hub use the paths below:

  • VST3: 
    C:\Program Files\Common Files\VST3\Slate Digital
  • VST2: 
    C:\Program Files\Vstplugins\Slate Digital

Some Cubase systems may use a Steinberg-specific folder or a custom path for VST2, for example:

  • C:\Program Files\Steinberg\Vstplugins\Slate Digital
Heads up: If VST2 is missing on disk, Cubase 13 and below cannot recall those instances. You will need the same format available for the session to load as expected.

Rescan Plug-ins in Cubase

Follow these steps to rescan all plug-ins:

  1. Open Cubase.
  2. Go to Studio > VST Plug-in Manager.
  3. Click the gear (cog) icon to open Plug-in Manager Settings.
  4. Click Rescan All.

Older Cubase versions place the Rescan control in a different spot:

Optional: Recover an Older Session That Used VST2

Most users should continue with VST3. However, if you are using an older version of Cubase (such as Cubase 10) you can ensure the VST2 format of the plugin is installed to your machine and scan it back into the DAW using the VST Plug-in Manager:

  • Complete Access Hub installs all formats by default. If you previously changed Preferences and disabled VST2, the format may be missing.

articles.title: Virtual Modules (VMs) - FAQ
articles.body:
Starting today, the modules from the Virtual Mix Rack (VMR) are being released as standalone Virtual Modules (VMs) that you can load directly into your DAW. This means you can skip the Rack when you just need one specific module, keeping your workflow quick and flexible. 🔥

This does not mean the Virtual Mix Rack is going away. VMR remains a powerful way to build, recall, and discover mix chains. With the release of VMs, you now get the best of both worlds: the ability to use the modules inside VMR and as standalone plug-ins.

All of this is included for subscribers, and perpetual license customers get both the VMR and Virtual Module versions of their purchases (retroactively applied to past purchases). Just open Complete Access Hub (formerly known as Slate Digital Connect) to install whichever combination you need.

We are releasing Virtual Modules in batches. The first batch includes Virtual Console Collection and FG-Stress, with more modules arriving weekly. Be sure to check Complete Access Hub each week for the latest releases.

More information can be found here: https://slatedigital.com/vmr-virtual-modules/

Frequently Asked Questions

❓ What are Virtual Modules?

Virtual Modules (VMs) are standalone plug-in versions of the modules from the Virtual Mix Rack. Instead of always loading the full VMR, you can now insert just the specific module you need directly in your DAW.

❓ Do Virtual Modules replace the Virtual Mix Rack?

No. VMR is still available and remains a core part of the Slate Digital ecosystem. VMR is best when you want to create, recall, or experiment with full channel strip chains. Virtual Modules give you a faster option for when you only need a single module.

❓ Is there a performance benefit to using Virtual Modules over VMR?

From our internal tests, CPU usage is about the same whether you’re using a single VM or the full VMR with just that one module loaded. The real benefit of VMs is workflow clarity and flexibility. For example:

  • You can see exactly which module is in your chain without opening VMR.
  • You can insert third-party plugins between modules more easily (e.g., insert SSL 4K G between a mic module and a compressor).
  • You avoid clutter when only using one or two modules.

❓ Can I move settings between VMR and the new Virtual Modules?

Yes! You can easily save and load presets between the Rack and VM versions:

  1. Save a preset in VMR using Save Preset As.
  2. Give it a name.
  3. Open the same module as a VM and load the preset.

This works in both directions (VM → VMR or VMR → VM).

❓ What’s a common use case for Virtual Modules?

One common use case is when you want to combine VMR modules with third-party plugins. For example:

  • Load a mic module (VMR or VM).
  • Insert a third-party EQ (e.g., SSL 4K G).
  • Follow it with a VMR compressor or a VM version of the same compressor.

Previously, this would require multiple VMR instances, which made your DAW’s channel strip unclear. With VMs, you can keep your workflow clean, and always see exactly which plugin is loaded.

❓ Who gets access to Virtual Modules?

  • Subscribers: Automatically get access to all VMR modules and their VM versions.
  • Perpetual license holders: Get both the VMR and VM versions of any modules they own, including retroactively for past purchases.

Simply open Complete Access Hub to install what you need. 👉 https://app.completeaccess.audio/installers   

❓ How will modules be released?

Virtual Modules are being released in batches. The first release includes Virtual Console Collection and FG-Stress. Additional modules will be added on a weekly basis. Keep an eye on Complete Access Hub for updates.

Still have questions?

articles.name: Missing Plugins When Loading Cubase Sessions (VST2 vs VST3)
articles.title: Missing Plugins When Loading Cubase Sessions (VST2 vs VST3)
articles.body:
If you're seeing errors when loading a Cubase project that certain plugins (like Virtual Mix Rack, Virtual Tape Machines, or Repeater) "could not be found," there's a good chance the issue relates to the difference between VST2 and VST3 plugin formats.

This issue can affect both Mac and Windows users but is especially common for Mac users on Apple Silicon systems due to additional factors like Rosetta compatibility and native plugin architecture.

✨ Common Symptoms

  • Plugin errors on project load, even though plugins are installed
  • Some instances of a plugin load fine while others show as missing
  • Manually reloading the same plugin works, but it doesn’t recall saved settings

📂 What's Causing This?

1. VST2 vs. VST3 Format Mismatch

Cubase treats VST2 and VST3 versions of a plugin as entirely separate. If your original session used the VST2 version of a plugin and that format is no longer available, Cubase cannot auto-substitute the VST3 version.

This situation often occurs when:

  • You updated Cubase to a newer version
  • You reinstalled plugins but skipped the VST2 format
  • You moved to a new computer and only installed VST3 versions

2. Apple Silicon (Mac) Specific Behavior

  • Cubase running natively on Apple Silicon does not support VST2 plugins at all.
  • VST2 plugins will only load if Cubase is launched in Rosetta (Intel) mode.

Also note:

VST2 plugins are not enabled by default in Cubase versions 12 and up. You may need to manually enable support: https://helpcenter.steinberg.de/hc/en-us/articles/22554401894162-Using-VST-2-Plug-ins-in-Cubase-14-Nuendo-14

3. Windows Users: VST2 May Be Missing or Disabled

Even on Windows, users can run into this issue if:

  • The VST2 version wasn’t installed (either deselected during installation or removed later)
  • VST2 plugin paths were not added in Cubase preferences
  • Cubase's plugin manager is set to only scan for VST3 plugins

✅ How to Fix It

If You're on a Mac:

  1. Try launching Cubase in Rosetta mode to enable VST2 compatibility
  2. Open the session again
  3. If plugins load, manually replace VST2 instances with VST3 versions

    • Keep in mind: plugin settings will not automatically carry over between VST2 and VST3 formats. You'll need to either manually copy settings or load a saved preset if available.

  4. Save the session
  5. You can now return to running Cubase natively with VST3-only plugins

Note: Intel Mac users do not need to use Rosetta mode. VST2 support should remain functional as long as the plugins are installed correctly and enabled in Cubase.

If You're on Windows:

  • Reinstall the plugin and ensure both VST2 and VST3 versions are selected
  • Open Cubase and check Plugin Manager > VST Plug-in Paths to verify the VST2 folder is being scanned
  • Reopen your session and check if the missing plugins now appear
  • Just like on Mac, you may need to manually replace the VST2 instances with VST3 versions and resave the session, being careful to copy any plugin settings over manually. 

    • Again, plugin settings will not carry over automatically — manually copy them or use saved presets

🔍 How to Tell Which Version Was Used

Unfortunately, Cubase does not display whether an insert was using a VST2 or VST3 version once it's missing. Your best clues are:

  • Whether the plugin shows up under "VST2" or "VST3" in Plugin Manager
  • Whether it's available when manually re-inserting
  • Session/project age: older sessions often used VST2 by default

🔧 Best Practices to Avoid This in the Future

  • Always install both VST2 and VST3 versions when available
  • When updating Cubase or reinstalling your system, double-check that legacy formats are supported and enabled
  • Consider updating old sessions by manually converting all VST2 instances to VST3 before future-proofing the project

❓ Still having issues?

If you're still running into plugin errors after trying the steps above, 👉contact our support team. Please include:

  • A screenshot (macOS/Windows) of the error message
  • Your Cubase version
  • Your OS and system type (Apple Silicon or Intel, Mac or Windows)
  • A list of plugins not loading

We're happy to help!

articles.body:
🔁 Compatibility & Access

Q: I own an ML-1. Do I get access to the new "Virtual Microphone System" plugin?
A: If you own an ML-1 (legacy mic), you can access the Virtual Microphone System plugin by subscribing to Complete Access or by purchasing the plugin license separately from our website. ML-1A owners receive a perpetual license automatically with their microphone—no subscription required.

Q: I own an ML-2. Can I use the new Virtual Microphone System plugin?
A: Yes, but only if you are subscribed to Complete Access or if you purchase the plugin license separately from our website. Note: The Radio France expansion is not available for ML-2 users.

Q: I'm a subscriber to Complete Access. Can I use the Virtual Microphone System plugin without owning a mic?
A: No. This plugin is designed to work specifically with Slate Digital's modeling microphones (ML-1, ML-2, and ML-1A). These mics provide the calibrated input and frequency response required for the plugin's emulations to be accurate. Using it without the hardware is not supported.

Q: Can I use the ML-1A with Virtual Mix Rack mic emulations?
A: Technically yes — but not recommended. Virtual Mix Rack does not include a "source" selector, and it's optimized only for the ML-1 (or ML-2 for Classic Instruments). Since the ML-1A has a different frequency response, the results will not be accurate.

Q: Can the ML-1A use the same mic models from the ML-1 expansions?
A: Yes — the ML-1A is fully compatible with all existing mic models from previous VMS expansions. However, please note that dedicated ML-1A versions of these mic models have been created to account for the ML-1A's updated frequency response.

When using the new Virtual Microphone System plugin, you can select your mic "source" (ML-1, ML-1A, or ML-2) to ensure the correct version of the mic emulation is applied.

Q: Will a source selector be added to Virtual Mix Rack?
A: There are currently no plans to add an ML-1A "source" selector to VMR. We encourage ML-1A users to use the new Virtual Microphone System plugin, which is specifically tailored for this microphone and offers additional features not available in VMR.

Q: Can I use the ML-1A with the original VMS One Preamp?
A: Yes, the ML-1A is fully compatible with the VMS One Preamp. While the new microphone models were not specifically designed with that preamp as a reference, the signal path will still work correctly. Modern interfaces with clean or neutral preamps will also provide a great match. We encourage users to try different setups and use whichever sounds best to their ears—any tonal differences are likely to be subtle.

🎙️ Radio France Expansion

Q: How do I get the Radio France Expansion?
A: The Radio France Signature Collection comes included with the Virtual Microphone System plugin license. This license is provided with the purchase of the ML-1A microphone, or it can be purchased separately from our website. The expansion is also available through an active Complete Access subscription. Note: The Radio France expansion is not available for ML-2 users.

Q: I don't see a license for the Radio France expansion in my account.
A: That's expected. The Radio France expansion is authorized via the Virtual Microphone System plugin license — there is no standalone product or iLok license for it. You will not see a product card for "Radio France" in your dashboard.

Q: Will the Radio France expansion be added to Virtual Mix Rack?
A: No. At this time, there are no plans to include Radio France models in Virtual Mix Rack.

📦 Purchasing & Ownership

Q: Where can I buy the ML-1A microphone?
A: Visit our Find a Dealer page to purchase the ML-1A. We'll be adding more resellers soon.

Q: Is the original ML-1 still available for purchase?
A: The ML-1 is still available while supplies last. It will eventually be replaced by the ML-1A. Support for the ML-1 will continue, and all hardware is covered under a 2-year warranty.

Q: I own an ML-1. Is there an upgrade or trade-in program for the ML-1A?
A: Not at this time. While we've considered it internally, there is currently no official upgrade program in place. We may explore options in the future, but nothing is guaranteed.

Q: How is the ML-1A different from the ML-1?
A: The ML-1A features lower self-noise, enhanced signal-to-noise ratio, new mic modeling tools like Proximity and Width sliders, and includes the Radio France Signature mic pack. For full technical comparisons, see:
👉 ML-1A vs ML-1 – Technical Specifications

Once redeemed, the license will be sent to the iLok ID linked with your Slate Digital account. Don't have one? We'll help you create one during the process.

Q: What software is included with the ML-1A?
A: The ML-1A includes the new Virtual Microphone System plugin, 12 mic models from the Radio France Signature Expansion, and every microphone model we release for the ML-1A going forward.

Q: How do I transfer my ML-1A to another person?
A: We recommend following our official transfer process here:

articles.name: Can I install my plugins or expansions on an external drive?
articles.title: Can I install my plugins or expansions on an external drive?
articles.body:
Running out of space? Many users want to install Slate Digital plugins and libraries to an external SSD—especially when using portable systems like MacBooks.

 macOS

On macOS, plugin installation paths are fixed and cannot be changed due to system-level requirements for how DAWs scan plugins.

Here are the default locations for each plugin format:

  • AAX: /Library/Application Support/Avid/Audio/Plug-Ins/
  • AU: /Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/Components/
  • VST: /Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/VST/
  • VST3: /Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/VST3/

These paths cannot be redirected to an external drive.

Note: Plugin files themselves are relatively small (around 10GB total if you install everything in the All Access Pass). Most disk usage comes from sample-based instruments and libraries.

✅ What can be moved?

VerbSuite Classics includes a large impulse response library, and we do support moving this to an external drive.

Follow the steps in this guide:

👉 How To Move VerbSuite Classics Expansions To An External HD on Mac

While this article focuses on macOS, the same principles apply to Windows. On both platforms, the default location for VSC libraries is:

C:\ProgramData\Slate Digital\VerbSuite Classics\Impulse Responses\Slate Digital\VerbSuite Classics

❌ ANA 2 cannot be moved

ANA 2 includes a large preset and sample library, but it currently does not support custom install paths.

We've passed this request along to Sonic Academy, but there’s no timeline for this feature at this time

🖥️ Windows

Windows offers more flexibility, but we recommend caution.

Note: If you're just trying to save space, moving plugin files is not always worth the trouble. Most Slate Digital plugins are lightweight. Instead, move large libraries (like VerbSuite) or uninstall plugins you don’t use daily.

🎛️ Plugin Formats on Windows

  • AAX: Fixed by Pro Tools, cannot be moved
  • VST2: Install path can be set in Complete Access Hub
  • VST3: Installed to C:\Program Files\Common Files\VST3 by default

If you want to change your VST2 install path in Complete Access Hub:

  1. Open Complete Access Hub
  2. Go to My Preferences
  3. Click Edit next to the VST2 Installation Path

Keep in mind: most modern DAWs like Ableton, Reaper, and Cubase allow you to scan a custom VST2 location (Windows only), but this must be configured inside the DAW manually.

Still need help?

If you're running into storage issues and want help determining what can safely be moved or deleted, submit a ticket here, and we'll walk you through it!

Understanding the Difference Between Your DAW’s Preset System and the Slate Digital Native Preset System

If you're having trouble finding presets in your Slate Digital plugins, you’re not alone! One of the most common sources of confusion comes from the difference between your DAW’s preset system and the plugin’s native preset system. Let's break it down clearly:

DAW Preset System vs. Native Plugin Preset System

Every DAW (like Cubase, Logic Pro, etc.) has its own preset system, typically found outside the plugin window at the top of the plugin interface. This area belongs to the DAW, not the plugin.

🔹 Cubase Example

Yellow Box: Cubase’s preset system
Green Box: Slate Digital's native preset system

🔹 Logic Pro Example

Yellow Box: Logic’s preset system
Green Box: Slate Digital's native preset system

🔹 Pro Tools Example

Red Box: Pro Tools preset system
Green Box: Slate Digital's native preset system

Important Differences:

    • DAW preset system:
      • Managed by the DAW (not Slate Digital).
      • Factory presets will not appear here unless you manually save your own.
      • Not recommended for saving plugin presets because it can cause compatibility issues across different plugin formats (e.g., VST2, VST3, AU) and different DAWs.
  • Slate Digital native preset system (inside the plugin UI):
    • Factory presets are installed and ready to go!
    • Presets saved here are cross-compatible across different DAWs and plugin formats.
    • Easy to export, import, and back up your preset banks.

If you want to move presets between computers, save them using the Slate Digital native system!
👉 How to Import New Presets

Why Can't I See Any Presets?

Some users write in thinking no presets were installed — but the presets are accessed through the native system inside the plugin! (except for Virtual Tape Machines, which doesn’t include factory presets). If you still can’t access presets inside the plugin, it could be due to a permission issue on your computer.

Troubleshooting Preset Access Issues

If you see an error like this when trying to save/load presets:



You'll need to update the folder permissions. Here’s how to fix it:

  1. Navigate to:
    Macintosh HD/Library/Application Support/Slate Digital
  2. Right-click on the Slate Digital folder and click "Get Info..."
  3. Set permissions to Read and Write for your user account.
  4. Be sure to "Apply changes to enclosed items."



If you’re using Repeater, Lustrous Plates, VerbSuite Classics, or an Eiosis plugin, you’ll also want to check:

  • /Library/Application Support/D16 Group
  • /Library/Application Support/Eiosis
  • /Library/Application Support/LiquidSonics

Summary

 

Special Note About ANA 2

One plugin that behaves slightly differently is ANA 2 by Sonic Academy.

If you're missing sounds or presets in ANA 2, you may need to reinstall the plugin manually:

articles.body:
If you encounter the following error message:

"Load Error: Could Not Load SlateCore"

This typically indicates a problem with how a plugin was installed or a version conflict between components in the Slate Digital plugin framework.

🎯 What Causes This?

This issue is commonly triggered by:

  • A version conflict between different Slate Digital plugins
  • A botched plugin installation, usually when the DAW was left open during install
  • Missing resource files or incomplete installs due to restricted file access during setup

Our SlateCore component is currently used by the following plugins:

  • Storch Filter
  • Fresh Air
  • Heatwave
  • Submerge
  • Murda Melodies

If any of these are corrupted or mismatched, the error may appear.

✅ How To Fix It

Step 1: Uninstall the Affected Plugin(s)

🔍 If you’re unsure which plugin is causing the issue, we recommend uninstalling all of the plugins listed above.

🖥 Mac Instructions

  1. Open Applications > Slate Digital.
  2. Open the folder of the plugin you want to uninstall (e.g., Murda Melodies).
  3. Double-click uninstall.command — this will launch a Terminal window.
  4. Enter your Mac user password (note: no characters will appear while typing) and hit Enter.
  5. Navigate to:
    Macintosh HD/Library/Application Support/Slate Digital/
  6. Delete the folder(s) for the plugin(s) you just uninstalled.

💾 If you’ve created custom presets, make sure to back up the preset folders to your Desktop before deleting them.

🖥 Windows Instructions

  1. Press the Windows key , search for Add or Remove Programs, and open it.
  2. Search for the plugin you want to remove.
  3. Click the three dots on the right, then select Uninstall.
  4. Navigate to:
    C:\ProgramData\Slate Digital\
  5. Delete the plugin folder(s) for the affected plugins.

🕵️ Note: ProgramData is hidden by default. Learn how to show hidden files in File Explorer.

💾 Don't forget to back up any custom user presets before deleting the folder!

Step 2: Reinstall the Plugin(s)

Reinstall the plugin(s) one at a time using the Offline Installation section on our Installers Page:
👉 https://app.completeaccess.audio/installers

⚠️ IMPORTANT: Ensure your DAW is completely closed during installation.
Closing your DAW also applies to Complete Access Hub installations.

Questions?

If you still run into issues after following these steps, feel free to submit a support ticket and our team will assist you further.

articles.body:
If you're a Complete Access subscriber and you're seeing that microphone modules like Classic Tubes, Classic Instruments, or the expansions (Strongroom London, Classic 87, Blackbird Mics) are not activated in Virtual Mix Rack (VMR) — you're not alone. This is a common point of confusion, and we're here to clear it up.

🔒 Why Are These Modules Unlicensed?

While your subscription does include the licenses for these microphone expansions, they require a base license called ML-1 to function. This license is only included with the purchase of a physical ML-1 modeling microphone.

Without the ML-1 hardware and its accompanying license, the microphone modules in VMR will remain inactive.

🔑 What Does the ML-1 Microphone Unlock?

Purchasing an ML-1 microphone includes a perpetual (non-expiring) license named ML-1, which gives you access to:

  • Classic Tubes (8 mic models)

  • Virtual Preamp Collection (FG-76, FG-73)

  • Free VMR modules: Monster, Revival, Trimmer

💡 Want to learn more about the ML-1 microphone?

🎤 What About the "Classic Instruments" Module?

The Classic Instruments module is exclusive to the ML-2 microphone. It also requires the corresponding license that comes with the ML-2 purchase.

articles.name: Is the Original FG-X Compatible with Machine-ID?
articles.title: Is the Original FG-X Compatible with Machine-ID?
articles.body:
With the recent addition of Machine-ID as a valid activation location for Slate Digital plugins through iLok, we've received a few questions—particularly regarding older, legacy products like the original FG-X.

If you're wondering whether the original FG-X can be activated to Machine-ID, here's what you need to know:

🛑 The Original FG-X is Not Compatible with Machine-ID

The original FG-X plugin is a legacy product and does not support Machine-ID activation. Even though you might see Machine-ID as an available location in iLok License Manager, that support only applies to the newer FG-X 2 plugin. Please see: https://slatedigital.com/legacy-products/ 

✅ Good News: Your FG-X License Unlocks FG-X 2

If you own a license for the original FG-X, you already have access to FG-X 2. You won’t see a separate license for FG-X 2—the same license authorizes both versions.

So while Machine-ID activation won't work for the legacy FG-X plugin, you can use that license to activate FG-X 2, which does support Machine-ID. More information about the free upgrade from FG-X to FG-X 2 can be found here ➡️ FG-X & FGX-2 Frequently Asked Questions

Reminder: We recommend using FG-X 2 for improved performance, updated compatibility, and ongoing support.

⚙️ Don’t See Machine-ID as an Option? Try This:

If your iLok License Manager doesn't show Machine-ID as a valid location, follow these quick steps:

  1. Deactivate your license from the iLok dongle:
    In iLok License Manager, right-click the ‘FG-X Virtual Mastering Console’ license and select Deactivate. This will free up the license.

  2. Find it in Available Licenses:
    From the View dropdown in the top menu, select Available Licenses to easily locate your FG-X license.



  3. Activate to Machine-ID:
    Right-click the ‘FG-X Virtual Mastering Console’ license and select Activate. You should now see Machine-ID as a valid location, along with iLok Dongle.
    Select Machine-ID and follow the prompts.

Once complete, you should see the activation reflected in the Valid Locations section, like this:


Still Need Help?

If you're still running into issues or have questions about your FG-X license, feel free to reach out to our support team, and we’ll be happy to assist!

articles.name: How To Move a License from an iLok Dongle to Your Computer (Machine-ID)
articles.title: How To Move a License from an iLok Dongle to Your Computer (Machine-ID)
articles.body:
Overview:
If you currently have your Slate Digital license activated to an iLok dongle and would prefer to use your computer (Machine-ID) instead, this guide will walk you through the process of transferring your license.

🔄 Step-by-Step: Moving a License from iLok Dongle to Your Computer

1. Plug in Your iLok Dongle

Make sure your iLok USB dongle is connected to the computer you’d like to use. This is mandatory to access and transfer the licenses.

2. Open iLok License Manager

If you don’t already have it, download the iLok License Manager here.

3. Locate Your iLok Dongle

  • On the left-hand sidebar, find your iLok dongle under “Locations.”

  • Click on the dongle to view all licenses currently stored on it.

4. Deactivate Licenses from the Dongle

  • Select the license(s) you’d like to move.

    • Tip: Hold Shift and click to select multiple licenses at once.

  • Right-click on your selection and choose “Deactivate”.

  • Your licenses will now move to the “Available” section of the License Manager.

5. Activate Licenses to Your Computer

  • Use the “View” menu at the top of the window and select “Available Licenses.”

  • Find the licenses you just deactivated.

  • Right-click each one and choose “Activate.”

  • This time, when prompted to choose an activation location, select your computer (Machine-ID) instead of the dongle.

  • Follow the on-screen prompts to complete activation.

💡 What is Machine-ID Activation?

Machine-ID Activation ties your license directly to your computer, making it ideal for users who don’t want to rely on a USB dongle or the iLok Cloud.

✅ Best For:

  • Offline workflows

  • Dedicated studio setups

  • Consistent plugin access with no internet required

🔒 How It Works:

  • The license is stored locally on your machine.

  • Once activated, you don’t need an internet connection to use your plugins.

  • Internet is only required for periodic tasks, like subscription renewals (e.g., Complete Access).

🔁 Need to Move the License Again?

To move the license in the future, you’ll need to deactivate it from the same computer.

⚠️ Note: Remote deactivation is not supported.

Still need help? Contact Support , and we’ll be happy to assist you!

articles.title: How To Move a License from your Computer (Machine-ID) to iLok Cloud
articles.body:
Moving your licenses from your computer (Machine ID) to an iLok Cloud session can be done using the iLok License Manager.

This process depends on whether your iLok Cloud session is in Automatic or Managed Mode. By default, sessions are set to Automatic Mode. If you're unsure which you're using, please see this article.

Make sure your iLok License Manager is up to date: https://ilok.com/#!license-manager

✅ Automatic Mode

  1. Sign in to the iLok License Manager with your iLok ID (if you haven’t already).
  2. Deactivate the license from your computer (Machine ID).
  3. Open your iLok Cloud session by going to File > Open Your Cloud Session.

🔧 Managed Mode

  1. Sign in to the iLok License Manager with your iLok ID (if you haven’t already).
  2. Deactivate the license from your computer (Machine ID).
  3. Open your iLok Cloud session.
  4. Activate the license from the Available tab by right-clicking or dragging it into the Cloud session.

🔑 Important:
Only the Complete Access subscription, microphone emulations, Fresh Air, and Heatwave licenses support iLok Cloud activation.
All perpetual licenses must be activated to a physical iLok 2 or 3 USB dongle or directly to your computer (Machine ID).

articles.body:
If you’re looking to activate your Slate Digital plugins directly to your computer (also known as Machine-ID activation), this guide will walk you through both available methods. Machine-ID activation allows you to use your plugins offline, without needing to remain connected to the internet.

💡 Want to learn about all activation methods including iLok Cloud and iLok USB dongles? Click here

What is Machine-ID Activation?

Machine-ID activation ties your plugin licenses to a specific computer. Once activated, you won’t need an internet connection to use your plugins.

✅ Best For:

  • Users who prefer an offline workflow.

  • Those working on one or two dedicated systems.

  • Reliable access without needing a dongle or internet.

🔒 How It Works:

  • License is activated to your machine and stored locally.

  • No internet is required after activation, except for license renewals for Complete Access subscribers

  • To move a license to another machine, you must first deactivate it from the original computer using iLok License Manager.
    ➤ Important: Deactivation must be done on the computer where the license is active. Remote deactivation is not possible.

Method 1: Using Complete Access Hub

  1. Open Complete Access Hub (formerly Slate Digital Connect)

    • If it’s your first time, sign in with your Slate Digital account credentials.

  2. Grant Admin Privileges

    • You will be prompted to grant administrator access. On Mac, this appears as a pop-up window asking to install a Helper Tool (see image below).

    • Enter your computer’s username and password to continue.

      👉Note: Windows users will see User Account Control (UAC)

  3. Activate Licenses

    • Click the blue “Activate Licenses” button.
      You’ll then see a screen like this:

  4. Choose “Machine”

    • On the activation location screen, select Machine.

    • This will activate your licenses directly to your computer.

Method 2: Using iLok License Manager

  1. Download & Install

    • Get the iLok License Manager here: https://www.ilok.com/#!home

  2. Log In

    • Launch the app and sign in with your iLok User ID.

  3. View Available Licenses

    • In the top menu, go to View > Available Licenses

  4. Activate Your License

    • Find the plugin license you want to activate.

    • Right-click and select Activate.

articles.name: Virtual Microphone System
articles.title: Virtual Microphone System
articles.body:
📘 User Guide (PDF)

🎙️ Introduction

The Slate Digital Virtual Microphone System is a breakthrough product that brings a growing collection of world-class and indispensable microphone models to your studio at an extremely affordable price. This amazing experience is realized through a combination of a specially designed and optimized ML-series microphone along with our Virtual Microphone System software plug-in.

To fully understand and maximize the value of the VMS, please take the time to read through the contents of this user guide. While VMS is fairly straightforward and intuitive to use, there are some points in this guide that will ensure top performance and results.

Setup

Your new ML-series microphone is set up just like any other microphone you may own.

  1. Mount the microphone to a microphone stand using the included mounting equipment. While it is possible to hold the microphone in your hand, mounting it will help ensure the microphone isn’t accidentally dropped and will also minimize undesirable physical noise that it could pick up due to handling and movement.
  2. Identify the microphone input on your audio interface that you wish to use, and turn its Input Gain all the way down. Note that the audio interface must be capable of providing Phantom Power on the microphone input in order to provide the microphone with the power required to operate.
  3. Turn down the Input Gain of the microphone input on the audio interface and ensure Phantom Power is off. This will help prevent loud noises when connecting the microphone. If needed, please consult the user manual of your audio interface to learn how to switch Phantom Power for the microphone input.
  4. Connect the microphone to the microphone input on your audio interface using a high-quality XLR microphone cable. You can use any cable brand or length you choose.
  5. Enable the Phantom Power on the audio interface. This will provide power to the microphone and it will begin to operate.
  6. While singing or playing into the microphone, slowly turn up the Input Gain on the audio interface. You should see the level meters on the audio interface begin to show an incoming audio level, though some audio interfaces simply have a single light that will illuminate when signal is present.
  7. Create an audio track in your DAW/host software and select the audio interface’s microphone input as the input for the track. This is now the track where your singing or playing will be recorded. As all DAWs function a bit differently, please consult its user guide on how to create a channel and assign an audio input.
  8. Load the Virtual Microphone System plug-in as an “insert” on the audio track.
  9. In the Virtual Microphone System plug-in, select your microphone model as the “Source Mic” in the upper-left corner of the plug-in.
  10. With headphones on, enable the audio track’s Input Monitoring. This will allow the audio being picked up by the mic to be heard in the headphones.

Usage

Now that the microphone is connected, operating, and the Virtual Microphone System plug-in is loaded in your DAW, you can begin to experiment with the various virtual microphone models available for your mic.

🎯 Initial Target Mic and Preamp Selection

Selecting a target microphone in the central area of the Virtual Microphone System plug-in will immediately apply that microphone’s characteristics to the incoming audio so you can judge how it affects the sound. You can switch to other mic models to hear different characteristics, and you can also change the Intensity and Proximity sliders in the plug-in to further customize the sound.

If you want to add further color and saturation to your recording, you can also choose to load one of the virtual preamp models in the right-most slot of the Virtual Microphone System plug-in.

🎤 Recording

Once setup is complete, you can proceed to record as you normally would with your DAW. The workflow remains the same as with any other microphone you use to record.

🔁 Changing the Microphone and Preamp After Recording

One excellent benefit of the Virtual Microphone System is that you can change the microphone and preamp models and their settings after you’ve made your recordings!

Unlike using a normal microphone, you don’t need to worry about which microphone model you choose at the time of recording or how the preamp was set! Oftentimes, what might sound good during the initial recording stages might not sound as appropriate during the mixdown stage of your project. If that’s the case, you can change the microphone and/or preamp model to something that is more complementary to your final mix.

Simply re-open the Virtual Microphone System plug-in and change the microphone model and/or its settings, and you’ll immediately hear the results of the new choices. Furthermore, since each audio track recorded with the Virtual Microphone System has its own unique instance of the Virtual Microphone System plug-in loaded on it, you can choose different microphone models, preamps, and settings for all of them!

Perhaps one microphone model gives the lead vocal the clarity and presence needed to sit in the front of the mix, while another microphone model softens a background vocal to sit comfortably behind the lead vocal and provide support. Feel free to experiment—the Virtual Microphone System provides ultimate flexibility and choice right up until you bounce your final mix.

Tips and Tricks

🎚 Setting the Input Gain on Your Audio Interface

When setting the Input Gain on your audio interface, do so when playing the loudest section of your performance. That is, a singer should try singing at the maximum volume or the instrumentalist should try playing as loudly as they intend.

While the performer is performing these loud sections, set the Input Gain such that the input audio level doesn’t ever exceed -12dBFS. While it is good to get the Input Gain set to a moderately high level, some amount of headroom should always be maintained as it is a common phenomenon that performers will still perform more loudly “in the heat of the moment” while recording compared to what they do during the initial practice and setup.

Therefore, keeping some headroom during the initial setup will ensure that these louder performances aren’t ruined due to overload distortion during recording. If you’re recording in 24-bit format, you can even be more liberal with your headroom (for example, not exceeding -20dBFS) without sacrificing audio quality.

Furthermore, input meters are often “slow” and tend to show an average input level. Very sharp (short and loud) transients can be missed by the meters but still cause distortion when your audio interface converts the analog signal into digital. Preserving recording headroom will help ensure that these transients are captured cleanly and accurately without distortion.

🎛 Setting the INPUT and OUTPUT TRIM in the VMS Plug-in

Due to how some of the microphone models behave, the output signal from the Virtual Microphone System plug-in can actually be louder than the signal going into it. Preserving some headroom when recording, as described in the previous section, will help prevent any overload in the plug-in.

However, if overloads do still occur even with the above precaution, you can reduce the INPUT TRIM slider in the Virtual Microphone System plug-in to add headroom and/or reduce the OUTPUT TRIM in the plug-in to reduce the level going into subsequent plug-ins in your DAW.

2️⃣ Dual Mic Mode

You can experiment with a virtually limitless number of microphone models by blending the characteristics of two different microphones to create a new hybrid behavior. Flip the “Single” switch over to the “Dual” position to expose a second microphone. Select another model for the right-hand microphone, and then use the Interpolate slider to “morph” the behavior between the two mic models.

🎚 Proximity

The Proximity slider can be used to recreate the “proximity effect” which occurs when the microphone is placed close to a sound source. This usually results in a boost of bass frequencies.
