Understanding License Activation Methods in Complete Access Hub

When activating your Slate Digital licenses for the first time, you have two options: iLok Cloud Activation and Machine-ID Activation. Each method has its own advantages and requirements, so it's important to choose the one that best fits your workflow.

1. iLok Cloud Activation (Cloud Session)

iLok Cloud allows you to access your plugins across multiple devices without needing a physical iLok dongle or tying the license to a single computer.

How It Works:

  • You can use your plugins on any computer as long as your iLok Cloud session is open.
  • An active internet connection is required at all times to maintain license authentication.
  • If the internet connection drops or the iLok Cloud session is closed, the plugins will no longer work until the session is re-established.

Best For:

✔️ Users who frequently switch between multiple computers.
✔️ Those with a reliable internet connection.
✔️ Quick and flexible access without dealing with a physical dongle or local activation.

2. Machine-ID Activation (Local Activation)

Machine-ID activation stores your license directly on your computer, allowing you to use your plugins offline.

How It Works:

  • Once activated, the license is tied to your specific machine and does not require an internet connection.
  • If you need to switch computers, you must manually deactivate the license from the current machine using the iLok License Manager before reactivating it on a new one.
  • Important: You must be on the computer where the license is active in order to deactivate it. You cannot deactivate it remotely.

Best For:

✔️ Users who prefer an offline workflow.
✔️ Those working on one or two dedicated computers.
✔️ Users who want reliable access without depending on an internet connection.

Choosing the Right Activation Method

Both methods are available when activating your plugin licenses through Complete Access Hub. However, consider the following before making your choice:

 

Additional Notes

  • Complete Access licenses come with two activations and can be activated on:
    • iLok Cloud
    • iLok 2 or iLok 3 dongle
    • Machine-ID (local host)
  • iLok Dongle Activation: You cannot activate licenses to an iLok dongle through Complete Access Hub (formerly known as Slate Digital Connect) at this time. If you prefer using a dongle, follow this guide:
    Activate and Use My Plugins with an iLok Dongle

articles.name: Slate Digital Plugins Do Not Work on macOS Sierra (10.12) or Earlier
articles.title: Slate Digital Plugins Do Not Work on macOS Sierra (10.12) or Earlier
articles.body:
Overview: Compatibility Issues with Older macOS Versions

If you’re experiencing issues with your Slate Digital plugins not working on macOS Sierra (10.12) or earlier, it’s due to compatibility limitations stemming from Apple’s discontinued support for these operating systems.

Apple officially ended support for macOS Sierra (10.12) and earlier on November 30, 2019. This change broke essential frameworks required for our plugins, making them incompatible with these systems. Below, we’ll explain why this happens and what you can do to resolve the issue.

Why Plugins Won’t Work on macOS Sierra (10.12) or Earlier

  1. Apple Dropped Support for Older macOS Versions

    • When Apple ended support for macOS Sierra and earlier, critical system frameworks were deprecated. These frameworks are essential for the functionality of Slate plugins, rendering them incompatible.

  2. iLok License Manager Requirements

    • iLok License Manager, required for authorizing Slate plugins, no longer supports macOS El Capitan or earlier. This makes it impossible to use our plugins on unsupported systems.

Minimum macOS Requirements for Slate Plugins

To use Slate Digital plugins, your system must meet the requirements outlined in the following article:

  • Supported Digital Audio Workstations

Although not officially tested, macOS 10.13 High Sierra is the minimum operating system that our plugins are expected to function on.

Is My Mac Compatible with macOS High Sierra (10.13)?

If you’re using an older Mac, you may still be able to update to macOS High Sierra. The following Mac models are compatible:

  • MacBook (Late 2009 or newer)
  • MacBook Pro (Mid 2010 or newer)
  • MacBook Air (Late 2010 or newer)
  • Mac Mini (Mid 2010 or newer)
  • iMac (Late 2009 or newer)
  • Mac Pro (Mid 2010 or newer)

To check your Mac model, follow these steps:

  1. Click the Apple  icon in the top-left corner of your screen.
  2. Select "About This Mac".

If your Mac is listed above, you can update to macOS High Sierra using the following link:
Download macOS High Sierra

Steps to Resolve Compatibility Issues

If you’re unable to use your plugins on macOS Sierra or earlier, here’s what you can do:

  1. Backup Your System

    • Before performing any updates, back up your system using Time Machine or your preferred backup method.

  2. Update to macOS High Sierra (10.13)

    • If your hardware supports it, update your operating system to macOS High Sierra. This is the minimum macOS version required to use Slate plugins.

  3. Reinstall iLok License Manager and Slate Plugins

    • Once updated, download the latest version of the iLok License Manager: Download iLok License Manager.
    • Reinstall your Slate plugins to ensure compatibility with your updated system.

What If I Can’t Update My System?

If your Mac or audio interface is too old to support macOS High Sierra, it will unfortunately not be possible to use Slate Digital plugins on your system. These limitations are caused by Apple’s changes to its software ecosystem, which we have no control over.

We recommend checking if an alternative system upgrade or replacement is an option to continue using our products.

Need Assistance?

If you have questions about your system compatibility or the update process, our support team is here to help. Reach out here with details about your setup, and we’ll do our best to assist.

articles.body:
If you've encountered graphical issues while using Slate Digital plugins like MetaTune, Infinity Bass, MO-TT, MetaPitch, Infinity EQ, Stellar Echo SD-201, or FG-X 2, this article will guide you through the troubleshooting process.

These plugins share similar internal systems, so if you're experiencing problems with one, you might encounter them with others as well.

⚡ Quick Tip: Most graphical issues are related to your graphics card (GPU) not rendering plugin graphics properly. We'll help you fix it step-by-step!

Troubleshooting Steps

1. Updating Your NVIDIA Graphics Card

  • Download and install NVIDIA GeForce Experience.
  • Launch the app and check for available updates.
  • Follow the on-screen instructions to install the latest drivers.

2. Updating Your AMD Graphics Card

  • Visit the AMD Radeon Driver Update page.
  • Download and install the latest drivers following the provided instructions.

3. Compatibility Check

  • If updating your graphics card doesn't resolve the issue, your GPU might not be compatible with these plugins (especially on older systems).
  • We've included a fallback option called CPU Graphic Rendering to handle visual processing with your CPU instead.
    • Note: Performance may decrease slightly in CPU Rendering mode, but the plugin’s sound will remain identical.

Enabling CPU Graphic Rendering

Follow these steps to enable CPU Graphic Rendering for Stellar Echo SD-201 (same process for the other plugins listed above):

  1. Insert Stellar Echo SD-201 into your DAW and open the plugin window.
  2. Close all instances of Stellar Echo SD-201 and fully exit your DAW.
  3. Locate the settings.xml file:
    • Windows: 
      C:\ProgramData\Slate Digital\Stellar Echo SD-201
      • Note: This folder is hidden by default. Learn how to show hidden folders.
    • Mac: 
      ~/Library/Application Support/Slate Digital/Stellar Echo SD-201
      • Note: This location is hidden by default. Hold the Option ⌥ key in Finder’s Go menu to access the User Library. See a GIF here.
  4. Open settings.xml in a text editor.
  5. Find the entry for UseCpuRendering.

  • Change the value field from 0 to 1.
  • Save and close the file.
  • Launch your DAW and reinsert Stellar Echo SD-201.

Helpful Links for Other Plugins

You can apply the same CPU rendering fix to these plugins:

articles.name: ARM-Based Windows Devices: Why Slate Digital Plugins Aren't Ready for Snapdragon Yet
articles.title: ARM-Based Windows Devices: Why Slate Digital Plugins Aren't Ready for Snapdragon Yet
articles.body:
🚀 With the growing adoption of ARM-based processors, you may have noticed new Windows devices running on Qualcomm Snapdragon chips, offering better energy efficiency and impressive battery life. As exciting as this sounds, there's an important caveat for professional audio users: software compatibility.
⚠️ Currently, Slate Digital plugins are not compatible with Windows systems running on ARM-based processors like Snapdragon. If you are a Windows user and rely on Slate Digital plugins, we strongly recommend continuing with devices powered by Intel or AMD processors.
🍏 Mac users — you’re all set! Slate Digital plugins work smoothly on both Intel and Apple Silicon (M1, M2, M3, and M4) Macs.
🧠 A quick tech refresher: ARM (Advanced RISC Machine) processors use a different architecture than the familiar x86 architecture found in most Intel and AMD-based Windows PCs. Originally popular in mobile devices, ARM processors are now making their way into laptops and desktops, bringing a mix of energy savings and new AI-driven features. 🌟 Windows Copilot systems powered by Snapdragon chips are leading this new wave.
🔧 We’re actively exploring ARM-based support for Windows in the future. But for now, to keep your audio projects running smoothly, we recommend sticking with x86-based machines.

📢 Stay tuned for updates, and as always, feel free to reach out to our support team with any questions!

articles.name: Troubleshooting Graphical Issues with FG-X 2
articles.title: Troubleshooting Graphical Issues with FG-X 2
articles.body:
If you've encountered graphical issues while using Slate Digital plugins like MetaTune, Infinity Bass, MO-TT, MetaPitch, Infinity EQ, Stellar Echo SD-201, or FG-X 2, this article will guide you through the troubleshooting process.

These plugins share similar internal systems, so if you're experiencing problems with one, you might encounter them with others as well.

⚡ Quick Tip: Most graphical issues are related to your graphics card (GPU) not rendering plugin graphics properly. We'll help you fix it step-by-step!

Troubleshooting Steps

1. Updating Your NVIDIA Graphics Card

  • Download and install NVIDIA GeForce Experience.
  • Launch the app and check for available updates.
  • Follow the on-screen instructions to install the latest drivers.

2. Updating Your AMD Graphics Card

  • Visit the AMD Radeon Driver Update page.
  • Download and install the latest drivers following the provided instructions.

3. Compatibility Check

  • If updating your graphics card doesn't resolve the issue, your GPU might not be compatible with these plugins (especially on older systems).
  • We've included a fallback option called CPU Graphic Rendering to handle visual processing with your CPU instead.
    • Note: Performance may decrease slightly in CPU Rendering mode, but the plugin’s sound will remain identical.

Enabling CPU Graphic Rendering

Follow these steps to enable CPU Graphic Rendering for FG-X 2 (same process for the other plugins listed above):

  1. Insert FG-X 2 into your DAW and open the plugin window.
  2. Close all instances of FG-X 2 and fully exit your DAW.
  3. Locate the settings.xml file:
    • Windows: 
      C:\ProgramData\Slate Digital\FG-X 2
      • Note: This folder is hidden by default. Learn how to show hidden folders.
    • Mac: 
      ~/Library/Application Support/Slate Digital/FG-X 2
      • Note: This location is hidden by default. Hold the Option ⌥ key in Finder’s Go menu to access the User Library. See a GIF here.
  4. Open settings.xml in a text editor.
  5. Find the entry for UseCpuRendering.

  • Change the value field from 0 to 1.
  • Save and close the file.
  • Launch your DAW and reinsert FG-X 2.

Helpful Links for Other Plugins

You can apply the same CPU rendering fix to these plugins:

  • Infinity Bass
  • MO-TT
  • Stellar Echo SD-201
  • Infinity EQ
  • MetaTune
  • MetaPitch

Still Need Help?

If you're still experiencing issues or have questions, feel free to reach out to our Support Team. We're happy to help!

articles.title: Troubleshooting Graphical Issues with MetaTune
articles.body:
If you've encountered graphical issues while using Slate Digital plugins like MetaTune, Infinity Bass, MO-TT, MetaPitch, Infinity EQ, Stellar Echo SD-201, or FG-X 2, this article will guide you through the troubleshooting process.

These plugins share similar internal systems, so if you're experiencing problems with one, you might encounter them with others as well.

⚡ Quick Tip: Most graphical issues are related to your graphics card (GPU) not rendering plugin graphics properly. We'll help you fix it step-by-step!

Troubleshooting Steps

1. Updating Your NVIDIA Graphics Card

  • Download and install NVIDIA GeForce Experience.
  • Launch the app and check for available updates.
  • Follow the on-screen instructions to install the latest drivers.

2. Updating Your AMD Graphics Card

  • Visit the AMD Radeon Driver Update page.
  • Download and install the latest drivers following the provided instructions.

3. Compatibility Check

  • If updating your graphics card doesn't resolve the issue, your GPU might not be compatible with these plugins (especially on older systems).
  • We've included a fallback option called CPU Graphic Rendering to handle visual processing with your CPU instead.
    • Note: Performance may decrease slightly in CPU Rendering mode, but the plugin’s sound will remain identical.

Enabling CPU Graphic Rendering

Follow these steps to enable CPU Graphic Rendering for MetaTune (same process for the other plugins listed above):

  1. Insert MetaTune into your DAW and open the plugin window.
  2. Close all instances of MetaTune and fully exit your DAW.
  3. Locate the settings.xml file:
    • Windows: 
      C:\ProgramData\Slate Digital\MetaTune
      • Note: This folder is hidden by default. Learn how to show hidden folders.
    • Mac: 
      ~/Library/Application Support/Slate Digital/MetaTune
      • Note: This location is hidden by default. Hold the Option ⌥ key in Finder’s Go menu to access the User Library. See a GIF here.
  4. Open settings.xml in a text editor.
  5. Find the entry for UseCpuRendering.

  • Change the value field from 0 to 1.
  • Save and close the file.
  • Launch your DAW and reinsert MetaTune.

Helpful Links for Other Plugins

You can apply the same CPU rendering fix to these plugins:

  • Infinity Bass
  • MO-TT
  • Stellar Echo SD-201
  • Infinity EQ
  • FG-X 2
  • MetaPitch

articles.name: How to Set Up MIDI in “Robotic” Mode
articles.title: How to Set Up MIDI in “Robotic” Mode
articles.body:
🎛️ About Robotic Mode

Robotic Mode in MetaPitch locks your vocal (or any audio signal) to a fixed pitch, giving it a signature "robot voice" effect. Instead of following the natural movement of the original melody, the pitch stays exactly on the note you set — either manually with the Note knob, or dynamically by playing MIDI notes.

By sending MIDI into MetaPitch, you can control the pitch in real-time, either by playing a MIDI keyboard live or by programming MIDI notes in your DAW. This gives you full creative control to choose the exact notes and melodies you want your vocal to follow, opening up endless musical and sound design possibilities. 🎶

Sending a MIDI signal to MetaPitch differs depending on your Digital Audio Workstation (DAW). Below are the setup instructions for the main hosts. 🎛️

Ableton Live

  • Insert MetaPitch onto an audio track.
  • Create a MIDI track.
  • In the MIDI track’s Output dropdown menu, select the audio track where MetaPitch is inserted, then select MetaPitch itself below.

Cubase

  • Insert MetaPitch onto an audio track.
  • Create a MIDI track.
  • Select MetaPitch in the Output section of the MIDI track.

Logic Pro

  • Insert the audio file you wish to process onto an audio track.
  • Create a new Instrument track and click the Instrument slot (not Audio FX).
  • Insert MetaPitch from the list of AU MIDI-controlled effects, then select your original audio track in the Side Chain menu (top-right of the plugin window).
  • Mute the original audio track so you only hear the output of the Instrument track where MetaPitch is loaded.

Pro Tools

  • Insert MetaPitch onto an audio track.
  • Create a MIDI track.
  • Set the Output of the MIDI track to the desired MetaPitch channel.

Reaper

  • In Reaper, you can superimpose a Media Item (audio file) and a MIDI Item onto the same track.
  • Add MetaPitch to the FX of this track.

Studio One

  • Insert MetaPitch onto an audio track.
  • Create an Instrument track.
  • Select MetaPitch in the Output section of the Instrument track.
  • If you’re using a MIDI controller, select your MIDI Device in the Input section of the Instrument track.

Questions?

articles.name: Install/update buttons have no effect on macOS
articles.title: Install/update buttons have no effect on macOS
articles.body:
Issue: Unresponsive Install/Update Buttons on macOS

Some macOS users have reported encountering an issue where the Install/Update buttons fail to respond when clicked in Complete Access Hub.

Possible Cause: Third-Party Audio Plugins

One potential root cause of this problem may be attributed to the presence of audio plugins sourced from developers other than Slate Digital. Certain third-party plugins have been known to interfere with a critical macOS software component called osascript, the AppleScript interpreter. This interference can result in unresponsive buttons during the installation or update process.

You can check whether the AppleScript interpreter is working by running the following command in the Terminal app:

osascript -e 'do shell script "echo osascript works"'


If you see the following error message, you're likely affected by this issue:

osascript: can't open default scripting component.


Solutions

Follow these steps to identify the plugin that may be causing the issue:

Make sure Complete Access Hub is not running.

  1. Open a Terminal window.

  2. Run the following command in Terminal:

    sudo fs_usage -w -f filesys osascript > ~/Desktop/usage-osascript.txt
  3. Enter your admin password when prompted. This command logs programs that use osascript into a file named usage-osascript.txt.
  4. Launch Complete Access Hub and try to install one of the plugins. If the install/update fails, you should have enough information for the next step. If the install works, restart the process from Step 1.
  5. Go back to Terminal and press Control + C to stop the logging process.
  6. Open the usage-osascript.txt file and search for repeated references to files ending in .component. You're looking for lines similar to:
/Users/<your_username>/Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/Components/<plugin_name>.component


Removing the identified <plugin_name>.component file may resolve the issue. However, multiple plugins can exhibit this behavior, so you may need to repeat this process for each suspected plugin.

If you've identified the plugin causing the issue and believe it should not interfere with Complete Access Hub, feel free to contact our support team for further investigation.

articles.name: What are the different modes in Infinity Bass?
articles.title: What are the different modes in Infinity Bass?
articles.body:
Infinity Bass offers four different modes to help enhance your low end. Each style is color-coded in the plugin, and we’ve matched that below! 🎨

🥁 Punchy (Bass Exciter)

Useful on basslines, kicks, or full mixes that need more punch, thump, or overall presence.

The signal below the frequency control is EQed, compressed, and saturated before being added back to the original signal. The Character blends saturation into the enhanced bass to help it stick out in the mix.

⚠️ Can boost low-end noise when used on older mixes.

🔥 Warm (Dual-Band Subharmonic Synthesizer)

Produces an octaver-like effect with lots of harmonics. Perfect for bass DIs or synths to add sub-frequencies and warm distortion.

The signal is split into two bands and a sub is generated from each. The Character control increases saturation for extra presence.

🎯 Works best on monophonic material.

🌊 Deep (Monophonic Subharmonic Synthesizer)

Clean sub generator with dynamics control. Ideal for adding missing low-end to kicks and basses.

The signal inside the selected frequency range generates a monophonic sub. The Character adjusts the decay and dynamics of the sub.

🌐 Can be used on full mixes if the low-mid range isn’t crowded.

🌀 Phased (Bass-Focused All-Pass Filter)

A sound design effect that moves bass content around, making it more resonant and smeared while lowering peak amplitude.

Only affects frequencies below the cutoff point.

🎨 Great for creating unique bass textures or strengthening weak transients.

articles.name: Powershell is not recognized
articles.title: Powershell is not recognized
articles.body:
In Complete Access Hub (formerly known as Slate Digital Connect), you may encounter the following error message:

🛠️ What's happening?

If you see the message "PowerShell is not recognized as an internal or external command" on a Windows computer, it usually means the PowerShell tool is missing or your system path is incorrectly set. PowerShell is normally installed by default on all Windows machines.

Solutions

1. Update Windows

In some cases, updating Windows can automatically restore missing tools like PowerShell.

2. Check If PowerShell v1 Is Installed and Recognized

Step 1: Open Command Prompt:

  • Press WIN + R → type cmd → press Enter.

Step 2: In the Command Prompt window, type:

echo %path:;=&echo(%

Look for a line that ends with:

WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\

If you do not see this, your Windows path will need to be manually fixed.

3. Check if PowerShell Is Installed

Open File Explorer and paste the following location into the address bar:

C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\

You should see a folder containing PowerShell:

4. Rebuild Your Windows Path for PowerShell

Step 1: Inside the Start Menu, search for:

Edit environment variables for your account

Step 2: Click on the Advanced tab, then select Environment Variables:

Step 3: Under System Variables, scroll down and double-click on Path:

Step 4: In the window that appears:

  • Click New.
  • Add the following path exactly:

C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\

Once added, click OK to save. Your system should now recognize PowerShell correctly!

5. Reinstall PowerShell (If Necessary)

If none of the solutions above work, you may need to reinstall PowerShell manually. Follow the official guide on the Microsoft Documentation.

Still Having Trouble?

If you're still stuck after following these steps, don't worry — just submit a support request and our team will help you out!
